title: Slide a circuit board into an antistatic bag held by the other hand
instruction: Hold the pink antistatic bag with the left hand, slide the green circuit board flat into it with the right hand until it is fully inside, then lay the bag in the grey crate and let go of it.
context: Refurbishers and e-waste triage lines bag thousands of bare boards for resale or storage. A board must go into its antistatic bag flat and all the way in, and a bag on a slick bench mat slides away when the board is pushed in, so one hand holds the bag while the other feeds the board.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are centres in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. Everything except the crate lies along one line on the table, turned 120 degrees from x (from front right to back left). Mat: a 24 x 28.2 cm dark grey rubber anti-static mat, 5 mm thick, long side along the line, fixed, centred at (0.29, -0.037), friction 0.25. Circuit board: a bare green 6.5 x 14 cm board, 1.6 mm thick with parts up to 2 mm tall (3.6 mm in all), 45 g, lying flat on the mat along the line, centred at (0.34, -0.124), parts up, its near end overhanging the mat's front end by 3 cm. Bag: a pink antistatic bag, 7.7 x 15.2 cm, 1.2 cm thick, 15 g, lying flat on the mat along the line, centred at (0.242, 0.046), its mouth (centre at (0.28, -0.02)) facing the board's far end 5 cm away, its closed end overhanging the mat's back end by 3 cm. Its cavity is 7.3 cm wide, 14.8 cm deep and 8 mm high, with a 3 x 1.5 cm thumb notch in the top layer at the mouth. Crate: a grey plastic crate, 25.4 x 17 x 7.2 cm (inside 24.4 x 16 cm), long side along y, fixed, on the robot's left at (0.30, 0.28). The bag and the board slide on the mat (friction 0.25) and grip each other (friction 1.0). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Measured at the end. The board's place is measured in the bag's own frame, wherever the bag lies. 0 if the board or the bag falls off the table (centre more than 2 cm below the table top). 1.0 (held 1 s) needs all of: (a) the whole board in the cavity (every corner past the mouth's line and within the side seams, its centre between the bag's layers, 2 mm of slack), its far edge within 1 cm of the closed end. (b) The whole bag inside the crate, resting on its floor: all four corners of its outline between the inner walls (24.4 x 16 cm), every point below the rim (7.2 cm), its lowest face within 3 mm of the floor and lying flat (its highest point at most 1.6 cm above its lowest). (c) The bag released: no gripper link touching the bag or the board (contact gap under 1 mm for 0.1 s). (d) The bag and the board still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s). 0.5: the board fully in as in (a), the bag anywhere else (held, on the mat, beside the crate, over a crate wall, above its floor, tilted, moving or still touched by a gripper). 0.25: the board's centre in the cavity (at least half of the board in). 0 otherwise, including a board on, under or beside the bag.
reset_notes: Take the board out of the bag and lay both flat on the mat as in the setup image, the bag's mouth facing the board.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The bag is a rigid stand-in for a soft one: one rigid body of thin box walls around a fixed 8 mm cavity, so it never opens wider, sags or folds. The board is one 3.6 mm box. Friction is 0.25 on the mat, 1.0 elsewhere. The crate is a SimReady model, fixed. Meshes are drawn, colliders are boxes. Grippers close with up to 50 N per pad. Release is read from PhysX contacts of all arm links with the bag and board (gap under 1 mm, 0.1 s). Masses are typical.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (ran to the step limit without finishing). Demo: 1.0 (success at step 409)
